svg.title: A research agenda, scored
svg.desc: LIA's research agenda: the eighteen-cutoff historical replay of Tshitoyan et al. with its three controls, the seven priorities scored by what the cases have shown, and the seven metrics with what each case supplies.
svg.text: EDGELESS LAB / LATENT INFORMATION ARCHAEOLOGY / PLATE IV-06-1
Seven priorities, scored by what the cases in this piece have shown
“The discipline should be judged by what it can demonstrate, not by the ambition of its premise.” The first priority has a worked example with stated limits, the second a
single case, the others partial results or none.
HISTORICAL REPLAY: TSHITOYAN ET AL. 2019, ABOUT 3.3 MILLION MATERIALS ABSTRACTS, 1922 TO 2018
corpus frozen: only abstracts published before the cutoff
each later year: share of the 50 since reported beside a thermoelectric keyword
Averaged over the runs, a top-50 material was this many times more likely to be studied as a thermoelectric within five years:
eight times, than an unstudied material drawn at random
three times, than a random material with a nonzero computed bandgap
THREE CONTROLS LIA NAMES FOR A REPLAY
Excluded by construction: each set of embeddings was trained only on abstracts
dated before its cutoff. A large language model's training text cannot be inspected
that way, and such a replay is not shown in these sources.
Fifty candidates scored at each of eighteen cutoffs, not one celebrated result, and the
The answer key holds only what someone went on to publish. Of the five top
predictions from abstracts before 2009, HgZnTe and SmInO3 had not been studied,
and score as misses either way.
Eighteen frozen corpora, cutoffs 2001 to 2018, scored against what was published afterward (Tshitoyan et al. 2019).
Baricitinib named in the Lancet in February 2020; the ACTT-2 trial, published in December 2020, reported a median recovery of 7 days
against 8. One candidate gives no rate, and failures need the same record.
Science4Cast ran ten methods on one task and curated network features beat end-to-end approaches (Krenn et al. 2023); an
expertise-aware model beat a content-only one (Sourati and Evans 2023). No matched comparison with domain experts.
Hsieh (2011) gives a mechanism, not a price. Larger corpora raised the replay's rate of successful predictions. Cost per defensible finding
has not been measured in any case told here.
Papers recognized late often mattered in other disciplines (Ke et al. 2015), yet each computational test here stayed inside one literature.
Abstracts emphasize positive relationships, and the time-sliced answer key has no entry for an association tried and found false.
Literature-based discovery has no comprehensive gold standard datasets. Science4Cast is one public benchmark for one field; the
excavation record of Chapter IV-04 is LIA's proposal.
USEFUL METRICS, AND WHAT THE CASES SUPPLY FOR EACH

and no estimate, so there is
“No single score can adequately represent all of these dimensions.”
Sources: Tshitoyan et al. 2019; Lancet letter, February 2020; ACTT-2, December 2020; Krenn et al. 2023 (Science4Cast); Sourati and Evans 2023 (abstract); Hsieh
2011; Ke et al. 2015; Thilakaratne et al. 2019; Findings of ACL 2024; LIA long-form, Chapter IV-06.
